title: Ecco: The Tides of Time
subtitle: Another journey through the ocean
summary: Ecco: The Tides of Time is Novotrade's underwater adventure, first released for Mega Drive in Japan on 26 August 1994.
body: Ecco: The Tides of Time is Novotrade's underwater adventure, first released for Mega Drive in Japan on 26 August 1994. Ecco returns to a world of ocean passages, unfamiliar creatures and threats connected to the Vortex. Swimming and exploration remain central, with air and health requiring attention as the dolphin searches for a route. The story also carries him into the future, where his descendant Trellia introduces another vision of life in the water. Travelling through time lets the sequel change the shape of the ocean itself.

Sonar serves several purposes. Ecco uses it to communicate, interact with special objects and inspect the surrounding area, while a charging attack lets him strike enemies and break through obstacles. Combining sonar with a charge extends his offensive reach. Some passages ask him to follow other dolphins through a maze; others involve collecting the scattered globes of the Asterite. Returning to the surface for air keeps exploration connected to the environment, so finding a promising opening also means judging whether Ecco can safely reach and investigate it.

Certain stages change Ecco's form, giving him the abilities of another creature for a particular task. Other sequences use a forward-moving perspective in which he passes through rings. The future introduces aerial waterways, extending the familiar act of swimming into spaces that seem impossible in the earlier ocean. These changes build variety around Ecco's movement rather than replacing it with an unrelated adventure. The Mega Drive music by Attila Dobos, András Magyari and Andy Armer supports a world whose beauty and unfamiliar sounds can make even a quiet passage feel uncertain.
